seoTitle: How to Recover Deleted Messages in Microsoft Teams (2026)
metaDescription: Undo a deleted Teams message, restore a deleted channel, and recover shared files from the right place: chat files live in OneDrive, channel files live in SharePoint.
intro: Accidentally deleting an important conversation or file in Teams doesn't have to mean permanent data loss, though the recovery path depends heavily on what exactly was deleted and how long ago. This guide covers catching the instant inline Undo option right after a delete, restoring a deleted channel as a team owner, recovering shared files from the right storage location, and when to escalate to an IT admin for deeper recovery through Purview. It's written for anyone who hit delete a little too fast and is now staring at a blank space where a message used to be.

steps.heading: Catch the inline Undo option immediately
steps.body: The moment you delete a message in a Teams chat, it doesn't vanish. It's replaced in place by a line reading "This message has been deleted" with an Undo link right next to it. This is the fastest recovery path, but Microsoft doesn't publish exactly how long that link stays clickable, so treat it as a short window and act on instinct rather than finishing what you were typing first. Click Undo and the original text reappears exactly where it was.

steps.heading: See how multiple deletions stack in a thread
steps.body: Delete more than one message in the same conversation and each gets its own "This message has been deleted" line with its own separate Undo link; they don't merge or clear out together. That matters if you're scrolling back through a chat trying to work out what's recoverable, because every deleted message stays marked individually rather than sitting behind one bulk-recovery option.

image.caption: A Teams chat thread showing two deleted messages, each with its own inline Undo link still active.

steps.heading: Recover a channel a team owner deleted
steps.body: For a deleted channel rather than a single message, the recovery lives in team management, not chat. Click the three-dot menu next to the team's name and select Manage team, then open the Channels tab. There's a Deleted section, collapsed by default; expand it, find the channel you need, and use the Restore action next to it. Microsoft's support documentation doesn't commit to a specific number of days a deleted channel stays recoverable there, so if it's already missing from the Deleted list, treat that as past the window rather than assuming a fixed date. Only team owners can see and use this option; a regular member needs to ask one to do it for them.

steps.heading: Know where a shared file actually lives before you go looking for it
steps.body: Files sent through Teams aren't stored inside the chat or channel itself, and where they land changes which recovery path applies. A file shared in a channel is stored in that team's SharePoint document library; open the channel's Files tab and Open in SharePoint gets you to the real folder and its Recycle bin. A file shared in a 1:1 or group chat is different: it's uploaded to the sender's own OneDrive, into a folder named Microsoft Teams Chat Files, and shared with everyone else in the chat through a link. There's no Open in SharePoint option for a chat file, because there's no SharePoint site behind it; only the sender's OneDrive has the actual copy, and only the sender can restore it.

steps.heading: Restore from the right Recycle bin
steps.body: For a channel file, use the SharePoint Recycle bin in the sidebar. For a chat file, the sender needs to open their own OneDrive, go to Recycle bin, and restore it from there; deleted items in either recycle bin are commonly recoverable for up to 93 days, longer than a chat message's own Undo window. Check the box next to the item and click Restore, and it reappears in its original location, still linked correctly from wherever it was shared.

image.caption: A file shared in a Teams chat, previewed inline with reaction and options controls on hover, the same behavior a restored file shows once it's back in place.

steps.heading: Escalate to IT for older or bulk recovery
steps.body: Past the recovery window, or if you need to reconstruct a whole conversation history for compliance or audit reasons, the Undo link and Recycle bin won't help; that needs administrator-level tools. Your IT department can run an eDiscovery search through the Microsoft Purview portal, which searches the Exchange data backing Teams chat and can pull deleted content well beyond what a regular user can see.

troubleshooting.problem: A shared file's Files tab has no Open in SharePoint button
troubleshooting.cause: It's a 1:1 or group chat file, not a channel file. Chat files live in the sender's personal OneDrive, not in a team's SharePoint site, so there's nothing in SharePoint to open.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask the sender to check their own OneDrive Recycle bin. Only they have a restorable copy; other people in the chat only ever had a link to it.

troubleshooting.problem: A deleted channel isn't in the Deleted section under Manage team
troubleshooting.cause: It's most likely past whatever retention window Microsoft applies before permanently purging it, which the company doesn't publish as a fixed number of days.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an IT admin to check whether the team itself, not just the channel, needs to be recovered instead, since only an admin can restore a deleted team.

faq.question: How long do I have to undo a deleted message?
faq.answer: Microsoft doesn't publish an exact duration for the inline Undo link, only that it appears right after deletion and doesn't stay clickable long. Click it immediately rather than continuing to scroll or type.

faq.question: Can I recover a deleted Teams channel?
faq.answer: Yes, if you're a team owner. Open the three-dot menu on the team, select Manage team, open Channels, and expand Deleted to find a Restore action next to the channel.

faq.question: Where are files shared in a Teams chat actually stored?
faq.answer: In the sender's own OneDrive, inside a folder called Microsoft Teams Chat Files, shared with everyone else in the chat by link. That's different from channel files, which live in the team's SharePoint document library.

faq.question: How long do deleted files stay recoverable?
faq.answer: Items in a OneDrive or SharePoint Recycle bin are commonly recoverable for up to 93 days, far longer than the chat's own Undo window.

faq.question: What if I need to recover a message older than the standard recovery window?
faq.answer: Your IT department can use eDiscovery tools inside the Microsoft Purview portal to search the underlying Exchange data and pull deleted chat content at the administrative level.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in July 2025. Undo, channel-restore, and file-recovery steps were re-checked against Microsoft's official support documentation in September 2026. That check found Microsoft doesn't publish a specific retention window for either the Undo link or deleted channels, so the earlier draft's invented "roughly 30 days" figure was removed. It also surfaced the more consequential correction: chat-shared files live in the sender's own OneDrive, not in SharePoint, so the previous "Open in SharePoint" instruction for chat files was wrong and has been rewritten to match how channel files and chat files are actually stored.
